The infinite-stream proof must not be presented as a proof about every finite soup encounter or every 6502 instruction family. **Width 3 has mixture writers.** The requested expectation “w=3 none” is true for the repeated-pair family in Proposition 9, and false for mixtures. The smallest returned mixture has primitive byte period 3 and execution period 6. ## 1. Proposition 9: corrected statement and proof State all of these assumptions: * A load has one opcode byte a followed by exactly w literal bytes L. A push has one opcode byte b≠a. No prefixes or intervening instructions occur in the repeated execution pair `(a L b)`. * Both instructions use the same data register R. Loading installs L verbatim; pushing preserves R and emits a fixed permutation π(L) of its bytes. The stack pointer is separate: neither the load nor the data value changes its addressing, and pushing changes it by exactly −w. * The executed byte stream remains `(a L b)^∞` over the part under discussion. Source mutation, virgin partner bytes, transient initial pushes and later overwrites cannot silently be identified with that prescribed stream. * Consecutive pushes occupy contiguous w-byte blocks. Reading memory in ascending address order reverses the **order of blocks**, not their internal byte layout. The copied region consists of these writes, with the same layout at every push and no holes or unrelated final writes. * For a finite copied window, require the corrected bound above. For infinite equality, no separate copy-length bound is necessary. Let E=`(a L b)^∞`, ℓ=w+2, and C=π(L). Every push has the same R, so the written stream in ascending memory is C^∞, up to phase. A copied N-byte window has periods ℓ and w. Fine–Wilf gives period g=gcd(ℓ,w)=gcd(2,w) at N≥ℓ+w−g. This bound is at least ℓ for all w≥1, so the window contains every residue of the execution period; the g-periodicity extends to all of E. For odd w, g=1 forces a=b, a contradiction. For even w, g=2 makes E alternate. Position 0 is a and position w+1 is the odd-position byte b, hence E=`(a b)^∞` and L=`(b a)^(w/2)`. The written block C must also alternate. Conversely, such an alternating layout emits a shift of E. For w=2 both permutations of the two bytes qualify. This is a sufficient construction for the prescribed periodic-stream model; completion in a particular encounter still requires its placement, phase, budget and bootstrap conditions. The original odd-width bound fails sharply in these examples (`a≠b`): &#124; w &#124; execution period &#124; literal &#124; ascending layout π &#124; output block &#124; matching window &#124; &#124;---&#124;---&#124;---&#124;---&#124;---&#124;---&#124; &#124; 1 &#124; `a a b` &#124; `a` &#124; `(0)` &#124; `a` &#124; `a a`, length 2; next bytes differ &#124; &#124; 3 &#124; `a b a a b` &#124; `b a a` &#124; `(1,0,2)` &#124; `a b a` &#124; `a b a a b a`, length 6; next bytes differ &#124; The second example includes a complete execution period in the matching window. `finite_bound_counterexamples.json` records concrete byte instances. An independent symbolic union-find check of all permutations, without invoking Fine–Wilf inside the algorithm, gives the following at the corrected bound. Every literal is a free byte, including opcode bytes; it is not sampled. &#124; w &#124; layouts checked &#124; layouts permitting a repeated-pair writer &#124; &#124;---&#124;---:&#124;---:&#124; &#124; 1 &#124; 1 &#124; 0 &#124; &#124; 2 &#124; 2 &#124; 2 &#124; &#124; 3 &#124; 6 &#124; 0 &#124; &#124; 4 &#124; 24 &#124; 8 &#124; &#124; 5 &#124; 120 &#124; 0 &#124; &#124; 6 &#124; 720 &#124; 72 &#124; &#124; 7 &#124; 5,040 &#124; 0 &#124; &#124; 8 &#124; 40,320 &#124; 1,152 &#124; For w=2r the count is 2(r!)²: each parity class of literal positions must map to one parity class of output positions. See `pair_layouts.csv` (46,233 layouts). ### Relation to Theorem 6 (H1)–(H3) Proposition 9 is best presented as an **independent structural lemma characterising when this restricted literal channel can realise (H3)**, followed by a conditional application of Theorem 6(ii). It is not a corollary of Theorem 6: that theorem assumes a self-consistent literal write and does not derive byte-width restrictions. The new result supplies that restriction. (H1) supplies default flow and the interpretation as an open program when execution reaches the partner. It is compatible with descending data writes; instruction flow and stack flow have opposite directions. It does not supply the partner coverage or execution budget by itself. (H2) is a machine-wide copy-cost hypothesis. Failure of a repeated literal pair, or even failure of all width-1 single-register literal mixtures, does not prove (H2). Memory copiers, stack exchanges, return-address writers and other families remain outside this analysis. No conclusion that every 6502 replicator must be closed follows from Proposition 9 or from the proof below. (H3) must be understood at the **executed phase of the tiling**, allowing the load–push macro and the emitted layout. Merely having an immediate load and a push is insufficient. The 8086 SP pair is excluded: loading SP redirects the stack, and original-8086 PUSH SP emits the decremented SP. In the zero-partner ring, even a legitimate literal channel can fail to bootstrap in one phase. ## 2. Census agreement and exceptions of scope Both repository Z80 lists agree: `review_r2/census_p2.csv` and `census6502/control_z80_words.csv` contain the same five nontrivial period-2 words. Their literal subset is exactly: &#124; word &#124; channel &#124; literal at the load &#124; ascending push bytes &#124; &#124;---&#124;---&#124;---&#124;---&#124; &#124; `01 c5` &#124; LD BC,nn; PUSH BC &#124; `c5 01` &#124; `c5 01` &#124; &#124; `11 d5` &#124; LD DE,nn; PUSH DE &#124; `d5 11` &#124; `d5 11` &#124; &#124; `21 e5` &#124; LD HL,nn; PUSH HL &#124; `e5 21` &#124; `e5 21` &#124; All three have the predicted alternating form and L=`b a`. The other two, `2a e5` and `e5 2a`, alternate too, but opcode 2a is **LD HL,(nn)**: its two following bytes give a memory address, not an immediate register value. They are memory-fed stack copiers, outside Proposition 9. Proposition 3 correctly groups them as load–push words; that grouping must not be reinterpreted as five literal-channel witnesses. `00 00` is the trivial already-zero fixed point and is not in these nontrivial lists. The requested temporary 8086 census directory was present. Its log lists 29 self-writers from 55,937 evaluated unequal-byte words, with 9,343 unknown words (256 equal-byte words were skipped). Its interpreter describes itself as partial and unvalidated; this audit establishes list agreement, not independent validation of the entire 8086 ISA census. Its **13 literal-channel entries** are: * load-first: `b9 51`, `ba 52`, `bb 53`, `bd 55`, `be 56`, `bf 57`; * push-first: `50 b8`, `51 b9`, `52 ba`, `53 bb`, `55 bd`, `56 be`, `57 bf`. All have `(a b)^∞` up to phase and L=`b a` at their load boundary. A push-first word begins with an initial-register push; the repeated load–push pair follows afterwards. **There are no nonalternating literal-push exceptions.** The remaining 16 listed 8086 words lie outside the literal grammar: `50 0d`, `ff 30`, `ff 31`, `ff 32`, `ff 33`, `ff 34`, `ff 35`, `ff 37`, `ad 50`, `c4 52`, `07 a4`, `07 a5`, `50 ad`, `57 c7`, `0e ea`, `35 ff`. They use arithmetic, memory/indirect operands, string copies, segment operations, stores or control transfer; notably `0e ea` includes a far jump. The absence of `b8 50`, despite the presence of `50 b8`, illustrates the bootstrap qualification. Replaying the supplied interpreter at its zero-partner settings produces `f8 50` repeated for `b8 50`, but an exact partner for `50 b8` and `b9 51`. The trace shows that later loads in the former encounter read altered operands: AX first changes from b850 to 50f8 at step 34. Both orientations of the SP pair (`bc 54`, `54 bc`) also fail. These are finite harness effects, not exceptions to the prescribed-stream lemma. `census_audit.csv` records all 39 source rows (the five Z80 rows occur in two sources); `census_provenance.json` records source hashes and replay outcomes. `8086_harness_trace.csv` records the concrete replay. No complete census was rerun, and none of these replays used a GPU. ## 3. Exhaustive symbolic search Here **k is an execution byte period**, so k=(w+1)nL+nP. Primitive byte period can be smaller: the w=2 witness has execution period 4, primitive period 2. Both counts are positive. Pure pushes with a preinitialised opcode-valued R would be a degenerate constant writer; that initial-state resource is excluded by the census's zero R and nonzero push opcode, and must be excluded explicitly in an abstract statement with unconstrained initial R. Every load operand is a free byte. An operand can equal any load or push opcode; there is no “operand alphabet disjoint from opcodes” shortcut. All token orders are considered, modulo rotating an execution cycle to start at a load. Loads and pushes use disjoint opcode sets, all loads set the same R, and all pushes have the same byte layout. ### Exact reduction and coverage through 64 For a candidate with execution period k and output-block period p=w nP, infinite equality implies code period g=gcd(k,p). The SMT search represents each of the g code bytes as a free 8-bit variable, all token orders as Boolean load/push choices, all register updates and the descending output order, and every output phase. Register state is cyclic; the first token is a load, so the concrete replay does not rely on an arbitrary initial register value. There is a complete reduction to **minimal decoder cycles**. If the input's primitive byte period is d, its next instruction is determined by its first-byte residue modulo d. A minimal recurrent cycle visits each such residue at most once. If its t=nL+nP instructions consume k bytes and emit p bytes, then d divides k and, for a self-writer, d divides p. Thus t≤d≤gcd(k,p)=g. Cycles with t>g can be discarded; repeated traversal of a cycle cannot restore an absent infinite-stream match. Distinct boundary residues modulo g are imposed on remaining SMT candidates. This is a proved symbolic reduction, **not literal enumeration of trillions of concrete words**. For width 1, g=gcd(k,nP)≤nP<t, so every minimal-cycle candidate is rejected. `minimal_symbolic_search.csv` contains **992 width-1 count cases through k=64, all UNSAT, no unknowns**. Their unreduced start-at-load token-order counts sum to 17,167,680,177,532; those orders are covered by the reduction, not visited one by one. The whole reduced run, including w=2/3 controls through k=16, took about 0.55 seconds on this CPU. Several distinct load and push opcodes are covered exactly. Map all load opcode byte values to A, all push opcode values to B, and other bytes to C. This map preserves instruction lengths, decoder boundaries, literal copying, and equality of streams. Any multi-opcode counterexample would map to a single-load/single-push counterexample. Therefore the single-opcode UNSAT result covers **any finite numbers of distinct load and push opcodes** with the stated shared-register semantics. No assumption prevents literals from mapping to A or B. A further direct SMT check, without collapsing opcode identities, uses load opcodes {01,02,03} and push opcodes {80,81}, all acting on the same abstract register: every count case through k=16 is UNSAT. ### Independent direct enumeration through 40 `direct_search.py` uses no Z3 and no minimal-cycle pruning. It recursively enumerates every load/push token order beginning at a load, then solves byte equalities with union-find. Opcode positions fix constants; literal positions remain free, and a conflict occurs only when unequal opcode constants are forced together. Code period g is imposed and all g output phases are checked. This is exact for the infinite-stream problem because both periods must divide the matching stream. **Width 1: none through execution period 40**, over **165,580,120** directly enumerated token orders, in **216.93 seconds**. The reduced search supplies the range through 64; the direct enumeration supplies an independent finite check of its conclusion. See `direct_search.csv` and `direct_run.json`. An initial unreduced SMT exploration was discarded because the proved reduction and direct enumeration gave complete, reproducible coverage; no incomplete or timed-out SMT result is counted as UNSAT. ### Width controls and the unexpected width-3 mixture The reduced control search through execution period 16 has 35 w=2 count cases (2 SAT), and 24 w=3 cases (3 SAT), with no unknowns. Each returned SAT model was independently decoded and compared over lcm(k,p) bytes. The direct enumerator through k=16 independently confirms these witnesses and also retains repetitions of smaller execution cycles. Full SMT constraints without the minimal-cycle reduction were cross-checked against the direct enumerator for every count case through k=16 and widths 1, 2 and 3; see `verification.csv`. * **w=2:** E=`(a b)^∞`; load `a [b a]`, push `b`. Execution period 4; ascending output `b a` repeated. Both layouts work, as Proposition 9 predicts. * **w=3, repeated pair:** no writer, under either infinite equality or the corrected finite bound; all six layouts were checked. * **w=3, mixture:** E=`(a b b)^∞`; execute `a [b b a]; b; b`. The execution word is `a b b a b b` (k=6). Each push writes `b b a`, so the ascending output is `(b b a)^∞`, a shift of E. **This is a counterexample to an odd-width prohibition for arbitrary mixtures**, not to Proposition 9. Every permutation of this literal has one a and two b's and is a rotation of E. More generally, for each w≥2, identity layout and the word `(a b^(w−1))^∞` execute a load of `b^(w−1) a` followed by w−1 pushes. The execution period is 2w, and every output block is a shift of the same period-w word. Hence the repeated-pair even/odd boundary does not extend to mixtures. ## 4. Proof of Conjecture 9′ in the infinite-stream model — PROVED Let E have primitive byte period d. Decode E sequentially using only one-byte push opcodes and load opcodes followed by one literal byte. At a token boundary, the next opcode and next boundary depend only on the current address modulo d, not on R: loads consume two bytes, pushes one. The finite graph of d boundary residues has an eventual directed cycle with t≤d distinct vertices. If the cycle contains nL>0 loads and nP>0 pushes, then nP<t≤d. Once the cycle has repeated, its loads reset the register in the same way on every traversal. The chronological emitted word per cycle therefore has length nP. Reading the descending stack in ascending order reverses that word, so the steady written stream has period nP as well. If the output is a shift of E^∞, then nP is a period of E. Every period of an infinite periodic word is a multiple of its primitive period d. But 0<nP<d, a contradiction. Thus no such width-1 periodic self-writer exists. A recurrent all-load cycle produces no unbounded output. A recurrent all-push cycle visits every byte residue (each step is +1), so E consists solely of push opcodes and the unchanged R emits a constant. This can match only a constant push-opcode word with that same preinitialised R, the excluded degenerate initial-state case. In particular it cannot match the 6502's zero initial A |
